# Container

<!-- Generated from the doc comments in the library. Do not edit this file. -->

A container element that supports padding, background color, and borders. Implements IContentContainer to participate in fluent API chains.

Namespace `BonniePDF`. Extends `BorderedElementBase`. Implements `IContentContainer`, `IStatefulElement`.

## Constructors

```csharp
new Container()
```

### `Child`

```csharp
IElement Child { get; set; }
```

The element placed inside the container.

### `ClipContent`

```csharp
bool ClipContent { get; set; }
```

When `true` and `CornerRadius` is positive, the container's content (background, border, and child) is clipped to the rounded-rectangle outline. This is what turns a rounded background into a true rounded-corner card: a full-bleed image or any overflowing child is masked to the rounded box rather than spilling past the corners. Defaults to `false`, so setting `CornerRadius` alone keeps the historical behaviour of a rounded fill/stroke with un-clipped content.

### `CrispEdges`

```csharp
bool CrispEdges { get; set; }
```

When `true`, the container's subtree renders inside a crisp-edge region: on SVG page export it emits `<g shape-rendering="crispEdges">`, so thin axis-aligned strokes and rectangles (grid/table lines, dividers) snap to the device pixel grid instead of being antialiased into a soft blur. It is a no-op on PDF output (the bytes are unchanged; crispness there is the viewer's job). Only wrap axis-aligned content — rounded rects, circles, diagonals, and text want antialiasing and will look jagged inside a crisp-edge region.

### `FillHeight`

```csharp
bool FillHeight { get; set; }
```

When `true`, the container takes the body content height left on the current page instead of sizing to its content. This is the primitive behind the header / body / footer page shape: the middle band is whatever the page chrome leaves over, a figure an author cannot compute up front because both templates are functions of the page number.

`Height` wins outright - fill is only consulted when no height is pinned - and fill never shrinks content: a container whose child is taller than the space left keeps the child's height and paginates normally. Measurement is unaffected (it reports the natural content height, because a pure measure has no cursor to measure from); only arrangement expands. Combines with `VerticalAlignment`: the slack fill creates is exactly the space it gained, so `End` anchors content to the foot of the band.

### `Height`


Optional fixed height for the container (null = auto-size based on content)

### `HorizontalAlignment`

```csharp
HorizontalAlignment? HorizontalAlignment { get; set; }
```

Horizontal alignment of the child within the container's available width. When the child is narrower than the container it is positioned accordingly; otherwise it fills the width as before. `null`/ `Start` keep the default left placement; `Stretch` is treated as "fill" (no offset).

### `Padding`

```csharp
Thickness Padding { get; set; }
```

Space between the container's border and its child, in points.

### `VerticalAlignment`

```csharp
VerticalAlignment? VerticalAlignment { get; set; }
```

Vertical alignment of the child within the container's available height. Only has an effect when the container is taller than its child needs - normally because `Height` is set - so it is the way to anchor content to the bottom (or middle) of a fixed box without hand-computing a top padding against a font's metrics. `null`/`Start` keep the default top placement; `Stretch` is treated as "fill" (no offset).

```csharp

```

Optional fixed width for the container (null = use available width)

## Methods

- [`GetChildren`](#getchildren): Returns the child, or nothing when there is none.
- [`Layers`](#layers): Fills this container with an inline z-stack.
- [`RenderStateful`](#renderstateful): Renders as much of the container as fits on the current page and reports whether it is complete or needs another page.
- [`ResetState`](#resetstate): Clears the continuation state, including the child's, so the container can be rendered again from the start.

### `GetChildren`


### `Layers`

```csharp
Container Layers(Action<LayersDescriptor> configure)
```

Fills this container with an inline z-stack. Layers paint in declaration order: `Background` behind, `PrimaryLayer` in the middle (it sets the flow height), and `Foreground` on top.

```csharp
new Container().Layers(layers => layers .Background(new Image("card-bg.jpg")) .Foreground(new TextBlock("Sample Company").Bold().FontSize(32)));
```

### `RenderStateful`

```csharp
RenderStatus RenderStateful(RenderContext ctx, float width)
```

Renders as much of the container as fits on the current page and reports whether it is complete or needs another page.

### `ResetState`

```csharp
void ResetState()
```

Clears the continuation state, including the child's, so the container can be rendered again from the start.
